english: Choose the correct sentence.
She has lived here since 2015.
She lives here since 2015.
She is living here since 2015.
She lived here since 2015.
An action that started in the past and continues now, with 'since' plus a point in time, takes the present perfect. The present simple and past simple do not combine with 'since' this way.
Complete: 'By the time we arrived at the cinema, the movie ___.'
had already started
has already started
already starts
was already start
The past perfect marks an action completed before another past action (our arrival).
Choose the form that shows an action in progress that was interrupted: 'I ___ TV when the phone rang.'
was watching
watched
have watched
am watching
The past continuous describes the longer background action; the past simple 'rang' is the short event that interrupts it.
Complete the third conditional (an unreal past situation): 'If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.'
would have passed
will have passed
would had passed
would pass
The third conditional uses if + past perfect, then would have + past participle.
Which sentence uses the indefinite article correctly?
She is an honest person.
She is a honest person.
It was an useful tip.
We waited for a hour.
'An' goes before a vowel sound. 'Honest' and 'hour' begin with a silent h, while 'useful' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.
Complete with correct agreement: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ___ informed about the change.'
were
was
has been
is
With 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the plural 'employees'.
Choose the correct passive form: 'The report ___ by the committee last week.'
was approved
approved
has approved
is approving
'Last week' calls for the past simple, and the report receives the action, so the passive 'was approved' is needed.
He told you, 'I will call you tomorrow.' A few days later you report it. Which version is standard?
He said he would call me the next day.
He said he will call me tomorrow.
He said he would call you tomorrow.
He said he will called me the next day.
In reported speech 'will' usually backshifts to 'would', 'you' becomes 'me' from your point of view, and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' when reported later.
Which adjective naturally collocates with 'rain' to mean a lot of rain?
heavy
strong
big
thick
English says 'heavy rain'. 'Strong' collocates with wind, not with rain.
Which verb completes the collocation: 'to ___ a mistake'?
make
do
take
create
'Make a mistake' is the fixed collocation; 'do' pairs with words like homework, research and business.
What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
to ease tension when people first meet
to end a friendship suddenly
to make a costly mistake at work
to start an argument on purpose
'Break the ice' means to help people feel relaxed at the start of a meeting or social event.
Passage: 'Although the drug reduced symptoms in most patients, some reported mild side effects.' Which statement is supported?
It helped most patients but had some side effects.
It helped every patient with no side effects.
Most patients stopped taking it early.
Its side effects were worse than the symptoms.
'Although' sets up a contrast: the drug worked for most patients, yet some had mild side effects. Nothing supports the other claims.
Which greeting is most appropriate in a formal email to a company when you do not know the recipient's name?
Dear Sir or Madam,
Hey there, team,
Hi guys and gals,
Dear valued friend,
'Dear Sir or Madam' is the conventional formal greeting for an unknown recipient; the others are informal or inappropriate.
In formal academic writing, which verb is the best replacement for the informal phrasal verb 'find out'?
ascertain
suss out
figure
dig up
Academic register prefers single-word Latinate verbs such as 'ascertain' or 'determine'; the other options are informal.
Complete: 'These results are ___ with earlier studies, which also found a positive effect.'
consistent
constant
considerable
consisted
'Consistent with' means in agreement with. 'Constant' means unchanging, and 'consisted' is a verb form that needs 'of'.
In academic writing, what does it mean to 'mitigate' a risk?
to make it less severe
to measure it precisely
to ignore it deliberately
to pass it on to others
'Mitigate' means to reduce the seriousness or harm of something.
The author ___ that the policy failed, but never states it directly. Which verb fits?
implies
infers
denies
proves
A writer implies (suggests indirectly); a reader infers (draws a conclusion). Confusing the two is a common error.
In a standard academic essay, where is the thesis statement usually placed?
at the end of the introduction
in the first line of the conclusion
at the start of each body paragraph
in the title of the essay
The thesis normally closes the introduction, telling the reader the essay's main claim before the body develops it.
What is the main job of a topic sentence in a body paragraph?
to state the paragraph's main idea
to list the sources used in the essay
to restate the essay title
to summarize the whole essay
A topic sentence, usually first in the paragraph, announces the single idea the paragraph supports.
Passage: 'Unlike earlier models, the new engine is light enough to be carried by one person.' What can you infer about earlier models?
They were heavier than the new engine.
They were cheaper than the new engine.
They were carried by one person.
They were built by the same firm.
'Unlike' signals a contrast in weight: if the new engine is light enough to carry, the earlier ones were heavier. Price and maker are not mentioned.
russian: 'В' describing location takes the prepositional case: в Москве. 'В Москву' (accusative) shows direction.
'Нет' meaning 'there is no' takes the genitive case: нет брата.
The indirect object (to whom something is given) takes the dative case: сестре.
An instrument used for an action takes the instrumental case with no preposition: писать ручкой.
Which phrase is correct for 'two tables'?
After 2, 3 and 4 a noun takes the genitive singular: два стола. From 5 upward it takes the genitive plural: пять столов.
In 'Мне нравится эта песня', which case is 'мне'?
With нравиться the person who likes something is in the dative, while the thing liked (песня) is the grammatical subject.
Complete: 'Вчера я весь вечер ___ письмо.' (focus on the process and its duration)
Duration ('весь вечер') calls for the imperfective past писал. Perfective написал stresses a finished result.
Complete: 'Я уже ___ это письмо, вот оно.' (the letter is finished)
A completed action with a result in the present takes the perfective past написал.
Which future form is ungrammatical in Russian?
Perfective verbs form the future with personal endings alone (прочитаю). Буду combines only with imperfective infinitives (буду читать).
What is the imperfective partner of the perfective verb 'купить' (to buy)?
The aspect pair is покупать (imperfective) and купить (perfective). Купать means to bathe someone.
Complete: 'Каждый день я ___ в университет пешком.' (repeated trips)
Habitual round trips use the multidirectional ходить, and 'пешком' (on foot) rules out the vehicle verbs ехать and ездить.
Which sentence means 'I am going to work by bus' (a trip happening right now)?
Я еду на работу на автобусе.
Я иду на работу на автобусе.
Я хожу на работу на автобусе.
Я езжу на работу на автобусе.
Travel by vehicle uses ехать, and еду is unidirectional, for a trip in progress. Езжу would mean 'I regularly go'.
The prefix в- means 'into'. Вы- means 'out of', у- means 'away from', and при- means 'arrive'.
Which suffix forms a noun for a person who does the action, as in 'учить' becoming 'учитель'?
-тель forms agent nouns: учитель, писатель, водитель. -ость and -ство form abstract nouns, and -ние forms action nouns.
What does the prefix пере- add in 'переписать' (from 'писать')?
Переписать means 'to rewrite'. Пере- often means 're-' or 'across'.
Which word is an adjective formed from 'зима' (winter)?
The suffix -н- with the soft ending -ий forms the adjective зимний. Зимой is an adverb, зимовать a verb, and зимовка a noun.
Which sentence with a что clause is punctuated correctly?
A subordinate clause introduced by что is separated from the main clause by a comma placed before что.
Which sentence with a который clause is punctuated correctly?
Книга, которую я читаю, очень интересная.
Книга которую я читаю, очень интересная.
Книга, которую я читаю очень интересная.
Книга которую, я читаю, очень интересная.
A который clause in the middle of a sentence is set off by commas on both sides.
Which sentence punctuates the introductory word 'конечно' correctly?
Introductory words such as конечно, например and к сожалению are set off by commas.
Which sentence with two verbs joined by и is punctuated correctly?
Он пришёл домой и сел ужинать.
Он пришёл домой, и сел ужинать.
Он, пришёл домой и сел ужинать.
Он пришёл, домой и сел ужинать.
Two predicates that share one subject and are joined by a single и are not separated by a comma.
korean: Which Hangul letter represents the 'm' sound?
ㅁ is m. ㅂ is b/p, ㄴ is n, and ㅇ is silent at the start of a syllable and ng at the end.
A final consonant (batchim) followed by a syllable starting with silent ㅇ moves over: 국 + 어 sounds like 구거.
Final ㅂ before ㄴ becomes ㅁ (nasalization), so 합니다 sounds like 함니다.
Final ㅌ followed by 이 becomes ㅊ (palatalization), so 같이 sounds like 가치.
Which ending is the formal polite style (합쇼체) used in news broadcasts and presentations?
-습니다/-ㅂ니다 is the formal polite level. -아요/-어요 is informal polite, -는다/-ㄴ다 is the plain written style, and -아/-어 is casual (반말).
Which sentence is appropriate when asking your teacher where they are going?
The honorific -시- in 가세요 shows respect for the teacher; the others are casual speech.
Which honorific verb replaces 먹다 (to eat) when talking about a grandparent eating?
드시다 (or 잡수시다) is the honorific for eating. 계시다 means 'to be', 주무시다 'to sleep' and 말씀하시다 'to speak'.
Choose the correct particle: '저___ 학생이에요.' (I am a student.)
저 ends in a vowel, so the topic particle is 는; 은 follows a consonant. As a subject 저 becomes 제가, not 저가.
Choose the correct particle: '책___ 있어요.' (There is a book.)
책 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이; 가 follows a vowel.
Q: '누가 왔어요?' (Who came?) Which answer is most natural?
New information answering a question word takes 이/가. 는 would add a contrast ('Minsu, at least, came').
Fill in: '도서관___ 공부해요.' (I study at the library.)
에서 marks the place where an action happens; 에 marks a destination or the place where something exists, 으로 marks direction or means, and 에게 marks a person receiving something.
What is the polite past form of 하다 (to do)?
하다 becomes 해 before -어, and the past adds ㅆ: 했어요.
What is the polite present form of 덥다 (to be hot)?
덥다 is a ㅂ-irregular verb: ㅂ changes to 우 before a vowel, giving 더워요.
What is the polite present form of 듣다 (to listen)?
듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, giving 들어요.
Which form means 'I will go' (a future plan) in polite style?
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 expresses a future plan. 갔어요 is past, 가고 있어요 is 'am going' and 가세요 is an honorific request or statement.
What is the basic word order of a Korean sentence such as '저는 사과를 먹어요'?
Korean is SOV: the verb comes last, and particles mark each noun's role.
Which phrase correctly means 'a big house'?
A descriptive verb modifying a noun takes the -(으)ㄴ form and comes before the noun: 크다 becomes 큰 집.
How do you say 3 o'clock in Korean?
Hours use native Korean numbers, and 셋 shortens to 세 before a counter. 분 is the counter for minutes.
How do you say 30 minutes in Korean?
Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers: 삼십 분. Native numbers such as 서른 are used for hours and ages.
How is the month of June written in Korean?
Months use Sino-Korean numbers, but June is irregular: 유월, not 육월. October is also irregular: 시월.
japanese: ぬ is nu. め is me, ね is ne and わ is wa; their similar loops make them easy to confuse.
How is the hiragana word きって (stamp) pronounced?
A small っ doubles the following consonant, producing a short pause: ki-t-te. A full-size つ would be read tsu.
How is 'okaasan' (mother) correctly written in hiragana?
In hiragana a long a is written by adding あ. The long-vowel mark ー is used mainly in katakana.
ン (n) and ソ (so) look alike, as do シ (shi) and ツ (tsu). The direction of the last stroke tells them apart.
What does the mark ー in コーヒー (coffee) indicate?
ー lengthens the preceding vowel in katakana: ko-o-hi-i.
What is katakana mainly used for in modern Japanese?
particles such as は and を
Katakana writes loanwords like テレビ, foreign names and some emphasis or sound words. Verb endings and particles are written in hiragana.
Which is the correct katakana spelling of 'taxi'?
Taxi is ta-ku-shi-i with a long final vowel marked by ー. ツ is tsu, and ダ is da.
Which kanji contains the water radical 氵?
海 (sea) has 氵 on its left. 林 is built from 木 (tree), 話 has 言 (speech) and 明 has 日 (sun).
The radical 亻 on the left of 休 (rest) and 体 (body) represents what?
亻 is the side form of 人 (person).
How is 人 read in 日本人 (a Japanese person)?
日本人 is read にほんじん, using the on-reading じん for nationality. ひと is the kun-reading used when 人 stands alone.
Fill in: 'わたし ___ がくせいです。' (I am a student.)
は marks the topic of the sentence; in this use it is pronounced wa.
Fill in: 'としょかん ___ べんきょうします。' (I study at the library.)
で marks the place where an action happens. に marks a destination or the place where something exists.
Fill in: 'パン ___ たべます。' (I eat bread.)
を marks the direct object of the verb たべます.
Fill in: 'だれ ___ きましたか。' (Who came?)
Question words such as だれ and なに cannot be the topic with は; as subjects they take が.
What is the te-form of のむ (to drink)?
Verbs ending in む, ぶ and ぬ change to んで in the te-form: のむ becomes のんで.
What is the te-form of いく (to go)?
いく is the exception among く-verbs: its te-form is いって, not いいて.
What is the plain past form of たべる (to eat)?
For ru-verbs, drop る and add た: たべる becomes たべた.
What does 'いま ごはんを たべています。' mean?
I am eating a meal now.
I will eat a meal later.
I want to eat a meal now.
The te-form plus いる (here たべています) expresses an action in progress.
A shop clerk invites a customer to eat. Which verb is the honorific (sonkeigo) form of たべる?
めしあがる raises the person eating. いただく is humble (kenjougo), used for your own eating or receiving, and おたべする follows the humble お...する pattern.
A receptionist politely asks a guest where they are going. Which honorific verb replaces いく?
いらっしゃる is the honorific form of いく, くる and いる. まいる and うかがう are humble forms used about yourself, and おいきする follows the humble お...する pattern.
german: Nouns ending in the diminutive suffix -chen are neuter, so it is das Mädchen despite the meaning.
Which gender do German nouns ending in -ung have, as in 'Zeitung' or 'Wohnung'?
Nouns formed with the suffix -ung are feminine: die Zeitung, die Wohnung, die Übung.
Sehen takes a direct object in the accusative, and masculine der becomes den.
The person receiving something is the indirect object in the dative; feminine die becomes der in the dative.
The genitive shows possession: masculine der becomes des, and the noun adds -s (des Vaters).
Mit always takes the dative, so masculine der becomes dem.
Choose the article: 'Ich lege das Buch auf ___ Tisch.' (movement onto the table)
Two-way prepositions like auf take the accusative for movement to a destination (Wohin?) and the dative for location (Wo?).
Complete: 'Ich habe ___ Bruder und eine Schwester.'
Haben takes an accusative object, and the masculine indefinite article ein becomes einen.
Which sentence correctly says 'I can swim well'?
The modal verb is conjugated in position 2 and the infinitive goes to the end of the main clause. 'Kann ich gut schwimmen' is word order for a question.
Modal verbs take no ending in the first and third person singular: ich kann, er kann.
What does 'Du musst heute nicht arbeiten' mean?
You don't have to work today.
You don't want to work today.
Nicht müssen means there is no obligation. A prohibition ('must not') is nicht dürfen: Du darfst heute nicht arbeiten.
Which modal verb typically asks for permission, as in '___ ich hereinkommen?' (May I come in?)
Dürfen expresses permission: Darf ich hereinkommen? Müssen is obligation, sollen is duty or advice, and mögen is liking.
Which sentence correctly uses 'aufstehen' to say 'I get up at 7'?
In a main clause the conjugated stem takes position 2 and the separable prefix moves to the end.
What is the past participle of 'anrufen' (to call)?
With separable verbs, ge- goes between the prefix and the stem: an-ge-rufen.
Ver- is an inseparable prefix, like be-, ent-, er-, ge- and zer-, so you say 'Ich verstehe' with no split.
Complete: 'Ich bin müde, weil ich jeden Tag früh ___.' (aufstehen)
In a subordinate clause the verb goes to the end and a separable verb is written as one word: weil ich früh aufstehe.
Which sentence is correct in standard written German?
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil bin ich krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil krank ich bin.
Weil introduces a subordinate clause, which sends the conjugated verb to the end.
Which conjunction keeps normal main-clause word order instead of sending the verb to the end?
Denn is a coordinating conjunction: '..., denn ich bin krank.' Weil, dass and obwohl are subordinating and move the verb to the end.
Which sentence correctly says 'I know that he can come tomorrow'?
Ich weiß, dass er morgen kommen kann.
Ich weiß, dass er kann morgen kommen.
Ich weiß, dass er morgen kann kommen.
Ich weiß, dass kann er morgen kommen.
In a subordinate clause the conjugated verb, here the modal kann, goes to the very end, after the infinitive.
Which continuation is correct: 'Wenn ich Zeit habe, ...'?
The whole wenn-clause fills position 1, so the main-clause verb must come right after the comma, followed by the subject.
chinese: The syllable ma changes meaning with tone: 妈 mā mother, 麻 má hemp, 马 mǎ horse, 骂 mà to scold.
How is 你好 (nǐ hǎo) actually pronounced in speech?
When two third tones meet, the first one changes to a second (rising) tone.
How is 不是 (bù shì, is not) pronounced?
不 is normally fourth tone but changes to second tone before another fourth tone.
In the pinyin qù (去, to go), which vowel sound does the letter u represent?
After j, q, x and y, the vowel ü is written as u without the dots, so qù is pronounced with ü.
Which radical is shared by 吃 (chī, eat), 喝 (hē, drink) and 叫 (jiào, call)?
All three actions involve the mouth, and each character has 口 on its left.
The radical 氵 in 河 (hé, river), 海 (hǎi, sea) and 洗 (xǐ, wash) is related to what?
氵 is the side form of 水 (shuǐ, water) and appears in many characters about liquids.
Which character contains the speech radical 讠?
讠 is the simplified speech radical, found in 说, 话 (huà) and 语 (yǔ). 打 has 扌, 妈 has 女 and 林 has 木.
In 十 (shí, ten), which stroke is written first?
the left half of the horizontal
the top half of the vertical
A basic stroke-order rule is horizontal before vertical when they cross, as in 十.
When writing an enclosed character such as 国 (guó, country), when is the bottom closing stroke written?
Rule: write the outer frame, fill in the inside, then close the frame with the bottom stroke.
In 小 (xiǎo, small), which stroke comes first?
For symmetrical characters like 小 and 水, the center stroke is written before the two sides.
Which measure word fits '一___书' (a book; 书 shū)?
本 is the measure word for bound items such as books and notebooks.
Which measure word fits '一___纸' (a sheet of paper; 纸 zhǐ)?
张 is used for flat objects such as paper, tickets, photos and tables.
Which measure word fits '一___车' (a car; 车 chē)?
辆 is the measure word for vehicles such as cars, buses and bicycles.
Which measure word fits '一___鞋' (a pair of shoes; 鞋 xié)?
双 means 'a pair' and is used for shoes, socks and chopsticks.
Which sentence correctly says 'I study at the library tomorrow'? (明天 míngtiān tomorrow, 图书馆 túshūguǎn library, 学习 xuéxí study)
Chinese places time and place before the verb: subject + time + place + verb.
Which sentence correctly says 'I am taller than him' using 比 (bǐ)? (高 gāo tall)
The pattern is A 比 B + adjective. 很 cannot go before the adjective in a 比 comparison, and 他比我高 reverses the meaning.
Which is the correct negation of 我昨天去了 (wǒ zuótiān qù le, I went yesterday)?
A completed past action is negated with 没 (méi), and the 了 is dropped.
What does 过 (guo) express in 我去过中国 (wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó)?
past experience: I have been there
an action in progress right now
a state that is still continuing
a plan for the near future: I will go
过 marks that something has been experienced at least once. Ongoing actions use 在 or 着, not 过.
Which sentence correctly says 'I have never been to Beijing'? (北京 Běijīng)
Experience with 过 is negated with 没 placed before the verb: 我没去过北京 (wǒ méi qù guo Běijīng).
In 他坐着看书 (tā zuò zhe kàn shū), what does 着 (zhe) express?
he reads while in a sitting state
he has sat and read before
he will sit down to read
着 marks a continuing state; V1 + 着 + V2 describes the manner of the second action: he reads sitting down.
ielts: Which IELTS sections are the same for the Academic and General Training tests?
Listening and Speaking
Reading and Writing
Listening and Reading
Writing and Speaking
All candidates take the same Listening and Speaking tests; Reading and Writing differ between Academic and General Training.
In IELTS General Training, what does Writing Task 1 ask you to do?
write a letter
describe a chart
write a lecture summary
describe a process
General Training Task 1 is a letter for an everyday situation. Describing charts, diagrams or processes is Academic Task 1.
How many questions does the IELTS Listening test contain in total?
Listening has four parts with 40 questions in total.
Which IELTS Listening part is a monologue on an academic subject, such as a university lecture?
Part 4
Part 1
Part 2
Part 3
Part 4 is an academic monologue. Part 1 is an everyday conversation, Part 2 an everyday monologue and Part 3 a conversation in an educational context.
In an IELTS Listening lecture, the speaker says 'Moving on to my second point...'. What does this signal?
a new main idea is starting
the talk is about to end
an example of the last point
a repeat of the last point
Signposting phrases like 'moving on to' mark a shift to the next main point, which helps you track where answers will come.
During IELTS Listening a speaker says, 'The meeting is on Tuesday... sorry, I mean Thursday.' What should you write?
Thursday
Tuesday
Both days
Either day
Speakers often correct themselves as a distractor. The final corrected information is the answer.
Which reading strategy means quickly locating a specific name, date or number in a passage?
scanning
skimming
paraphrasing
summarizing
Scanning searches for specific details. Skimming is a fast read for the general idea.
In IELTS Reading, when should you answer Not Given to a True/False/Not Given statement?
when the passage neither confirms nor contradicts it
when the statement is only partly true
when the passage directly contradicts the statement
when the statement seems unlikely to be true
Not Given means the text has no information either way. If the text contradicts the statement, the answer is False.
Passage: 'The museum, which opened in 1990, attracts over a million visitors a year.' Statement: 'It was the first museum in the city.' What is the answer?
Not Given
True
False
Partly True
The passage says nothing about other museums in the city, so the statement can be neither confirmed nor contradicted.
Passage: 'Unlike most birds, the kiwi cannot fly.' Statement: 'The kiwi is able to fly.' What is the answer?
False
True
Not Given
Yes
The passage directly contradicts the statement, so the answer is False.
How do Yes/No/Not Given questions differ from True/False/Not Given questions in IELTS Reading?
they ask about the writer's views or claims
they ask only about numbers and dates
they use only diagrams and tables
they test definitions of vocabulary
True/False/Not Given checks factual information, while Yes/No/Not Given checks whether statements agree with the writer's opinions or claims.
What is the minimum word count for IELTS Academic Writing Task 1?
150 words
250 words
100 words
200 words
Task 1 requires at least 150 words; Task 2 requires at least 250.
Which element is essential in an IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 chart description?
an overview of the main trends
your opinion on the causes
every single data point
a recommendation for action
Examiners look for a clear overview of the key features. Personal opinions are not required in Task 1.
A line graph shows sales rising from 20 to 80 units. Which sentence best describes it in Task 1 style?
Sales quadrupled, rising from 20 to 80 units.
Sales doubled, rising from 20 to 80 units.
Sales rose because demand clearly grew.
Sales were good and then got even better.
From 20 to 80 is a fourfold increase. Task 1 reports data accurately and does not speculate about causes.
What is the minimum word count for IELTS Writing Task 2?
250 words
150 words
300 words
200 words
Task 2 requires at least 250 words.
Which IELTS writing task carries more weight in the Writing score?
Task 2
Task 1
Both equally
The longer one
Task 2 counts for twice as much as Task 1, so it deserves about 40 of the 60 minutes.
Task 2 prompt: 'University education should be free. To what extent do you agree?' Which is the best thesis sentence?
I largely agree, as free tuition widens access, though costs could be shared.
University education is a topic that many people around the world discuss nowadays.
There are many advantages and disadvantages to this issue for students.
In this essay I will talk about universities and the fees that they charge.
A strong thesis answers the question directly and previews the reasoning. The others are vague and take no position.
In IELTS Speaking Part 2, how long do you get to prepare before speaking on the cue card topic?
1 minute
30 seconds
2 minutes
5 minutes
You get one minute to prepare and make notes, then speak for up to two minutes.
Which is NOT one of the four IELTS Speaking assessment criteria?
Task Achievement
Fluency and Coherence
Lexical Resource
Pronunciation
Speaking is assessed on Fluency and Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy, and Pronunciation. Task Achievement is a Writing Task 1 criterion.
In IELTS Speaking Part 1 the examiner asks, 'Do you like reading?' Which answer is best?
Yes, especially novels; they help me relax after classes.
Yes, I do, and I think that is all I can say about it.
Yes, I like reading, I like books, I like it a lot.
Reading is a popular hobby all over the world.
A good Part 1 answer is direct and extended with a reason or example. Repetition and generic statements do not show range.
toefl: In the TOEFL iBT Integrated Writing task, how does the lecture usually relate to the reading passage?
it challenges or casts doubt on the reading
it repeats the reading in simpler words
it introduces an unrelated topic
it gives the student's own opinion
In the typical task the lecturer responds point by point to the reading, usually by challenging its claims.
What is the main goal of a TOEFL Integrated Writing response?
explain how the lecture responds to the reading
give your own opinion on the topic of the reading
summarize only the reading passage in detail
add new examples from your own life to the topic
The task asks you to summarize the lecture's points and show how they relate to the reading. Personal opinion is not wanted.
Which is the best opening sentence for a TOEFL Integrated Writing response?
The lecturer argues that the reading's three theories are unconvincing.
I strongly believe that the reading passage is correct in every way.
This topic is very interesting for many people in the world today.
In my country, this problem is very common nowadays among young people.
It states the relationship between the lecture and the reading, which is the whole task. The others give opinion or filler.
Which phrase best links a lecture point to the reading in an Integrated Writing response?
This casts doubt on the reading's claim that
In my own personal experience, I think that
To sum up all of my personal feelings,
As everyone in the world already knows,
Integrated Writing is about connecting sources, so a link that ties the lecture to a specific reading claim is best.
Who typically speaks in a TOEFL iBT Listening conversation?
a student and a professor or campus staff member
two business partners discussing a deal on a phone call
a job applicant and a company manager in an interview
a news anchor reporting on world events
TOEFL conversations are set in university life, such as office hours or a visit to a campus service office.
Can you take notes during the TOEFL iBT Listening section?
Yes, note-taking is allowed
No, note-taking is not permitted
Only during lectures
Only after each recording ends
TOEFL allows notes throughout, and good notes on main ideas and examples help with detail and organization questions.
A lecturer says, 'Now, this is the crucial point...'. Why does this matter in TOEFL Listening?
it signals information likely to be tested
it signals that the lecture is about to end
it marks a joke that you can safely ignore
it introduces an off-topic personal story
Emphasis phrases highlight main ideas, which questions often target.
A TOEFL Listening question asks why the professor mentions a story about her own garden. What type of question is this?
a function or purpose question
a vocabulary question
a detail question about numbers
a prose summary question
Function questions ask why a speaker says something, such as to give an example or illustrate a concept.
A professor says, 'Some argue this theory is outdated, but I'm not so sure.' What is her attitude?
doubtful that the theory is outdated
convinced that the theory is outdated
uninterested in the theory
angry at the theory's supporters
'I'm not so sure' signals doubt about the claim that the theory is outdated. Attitude questions test this kind of cue.
What should a strong TOEFL independent speaking response include?
a clear opinion with reasons and an example
both sides of the issue with no final opinion
a long restatement of the question itself
a memorized story that is off the topic
Raters reward a clear position developed with specific reasons and examples in the short time available.
Prompt: 'Do you prefer studying alone or in a group?' Which is the best opening sentence?
I prefer studying alone, mainly because I focus better without distractions.
Studying is very important for all students everywhere, so both ways are good.
Some people like studying in groups and some people like being alone.
This is a hard question and I have not really thought about it before.
It states a clear preference and a reason immediately, giving the response a direction.
Only a few seconds remain in a TOEFL speaking response. What is the best use of that time?
a short sentence restating your view
starting a brand-new example
repeating the question word for word
stopping and waiting in silence
A brief wrap-up keeps the response complete and coherent. A new example would be cut off.
In a TOEFL campus-situation integrated speaking task, what do you typically do?
report a student's opinion of a plan and the reasons
describe your own campus and the facilities it offers
give your own opinion on the campus announcement
read the announcement aloud to the rater clearly
You read a short campus text, hear students discuss it, and then explain the speaker's opinion and reasons.
In an academic integrated speaking task, how should you use the professor's example?
explain how it illustrates the concept from the reading
replace it with a more interesting example from your own experience
skip it and only define the concept from the reading
criticize the professor's choice of it as an example
The task tests whether you can connect the general concept in the reading to the specific example in the lecture.
Which note-taking approach works best for TOEFL integrated speaking tasks?
key words split into reading and listening columns
writing down every single word the speaker says
taking no notes at all in order to stay fully focused
noting only the first sentence of each source
Brief, organized notes let you find each source's key points quickly during the short preparation time.
A TOEFL Reading question says, 'All of the following are mentioned in the paragraph EXCEPT'. What type is it?
negative factual information
inference from implied information
rhetorical purpose of a detail
vocabulary meaning in context
EXCEPT and NOT questions are negative factual information items: three options appear in the text and one does not.
What do you do in a TOEFL Reading prose summary question?
choose the options that express the major ideas
pick sentences with exact words from the text
write a short summary in your own words
put the paragraphs of the passage back in time order
Prose summary items ask you to select the answer choices that capture the passage's most important ideas, not minor details.
In a TOEFL Reading insert-text question, what is the best clue for placing the sentence?
linking words and pronouns that connect to nearby sentences
the length of the sentence compared with the ones nearby
where the paragraph appears on the screen during the test
how many squares the paragraph has, choosing the middle one
Words like 'this', 'however' or 'these changes' must refer back to something just before them.
Passage: 'The species declined after the dam was built, which blocked its migration route.' What can be inferred?
the dam likely contributed to the decline
the species had no migration route
the dam was built to protect the species
the species grew after the dam was built
The passage links the dam to a blocked migration route and the decline that followed, so a causal role is the reasonable inference.
In the sentence 'Fish were abundant in the lake', what does 'abundant' mean?
plentiful
rare
dangerous
colorful
'Abundant' means present in large quantities. TOEFL vocabulary items test meaning in context.
